name: recursive side-condition discharge: a conditional rule's hypotheses are proved by running the same simplifier on them, depth-bounded, with the memo table protected

questions.ancestry: Lean 4 simp. The discharger slot is a Methods field; the DEFAULT discharger is simp itself. Found by reading synthesizeArgs and asking what proves the Prop arguments; the boundary coincides with defs dischargeDefault? and discharge?'.
questions.mechanism: When a rule matched but has hypotheses left as metavariables, each instance-implicit one is solved by type-class synthesis and checked defeq to what unification assigned (57-107); each Prop one is handed to the discharger. The default discharger runs the whole simplifier on the hypothesis; success is 'it became True' or 'it became an equation provable by rfl'. Depth is capped by maxDischargeDepth; the memo cache is snapshotted and restored around the call (withPreservedCache) and the used-theorem set is rolled back on failure so failed attempts leave no trace.
questions.input: a hypothesis type (Prop), the current context and methods, the depth counter
questions.output: Option Expr: a proof term, or none; side effect: the rule is not applied if any hypothesis fails
questions.state: the memo cache (protected by snapshot/restore), the discharge depth counter, the usedTheorems set (rolled back); AND the local context: a discharger that uses hypotheses introduced during the run makes cached results context-dependent, which is exactly what the wellBehavedDischarge flag declares (Types.lean 426-433) -- the hidden state this organ carries
questions.assumptions: that the same normaliser that rewrites the goal is a good prover for side conditions; that 'reaches True' is the right success criterion; that a depth cap is an acceptable substitute for a termination argument; that instance arguments must be checked defeq to the unifier's choice (the comment at 66-83 records that a stricter check was tried and abandoned)
questions.interface: discharge?(hyp: Expr) -> SimpM (Option Expr), pluggable (Methods.discharge?); the tactic can supply any TacticM discharger (Elab/Tactic/Simp.lean 37-63 tacticToDischarge) at the price of wellBehavedDischarge := false
questions.fitness_value: Conditional rewrite rules (x / x = 1 if x != 0) are usable without the user proving each side condition; the self-call means the store's own facts prove the store's own conditions. Claimed; how often the default discharger succeeds vs falls back is instrumented (trace Meta.Tactic.simp.discharge) but not measured here.
questions.failure_landscape: (a) depth exhaustion returns notProved silently: a rule that needed depth 3 when the cap is 2 just does not fire, indistinguishable from 'condition false'; (b) recursive self-call means side-condition cost is unbounded by the goal's size; (c) the caching contract is by DECLARATION (wellBehavedDischarge) not by check -- a user discharger that lies gets wrong cached results; (d) instance defeq failures are a known pain point (comment 66-83) and were relaxed for convenience, which is a soundness-preserving but completeness-affecting policy.
questions.ablation: Designed, not measured: replace the default discharger by fun _ => none. Prediction: every conditional rule stops firing; unconditional rewriting is unaffected. A second, sharper ablation: cap maxDischargeDepth at 0 vs 1 vs 2 and count fired conditional rules on a fixture -- the depth-hidden failures become visible.
questions.decomposability: Into (1) the slot (a function-typed field: SCAFFOLDING), (2) the default strategy 'normalise the hypothesis and accept True' (the mechanism), (3) the state-protection discipline around the call (belongs to c14 memo-validity). The record is (2)+(3) at CUT-1; CUT-2 may split them.
questions.composability: Any rule engine with conditional rules; the pattern 'the engine is its own side-condition prover, depth-bounded' transfers to any Prometheus organism that has rules with guards. Archaeon's H3 behavioural rules have no guards today, so no live consumer; recorded.
questions.human_prior: That side conditions are 'easy' relative to the goal (hence the same tool suffices and a small depth cap is fine); that soundness is non-negotiable while completeness is tunable (the depth cap, the relaxed instance check).
questions.control: Positive: a conditional rule whose hypothesis simplifies to True in one step fires at depth >= 1. Negative: the same rule with a false hypothesis never fires (and the result is unchanged, not wrong). Cheat control: a discharger that returns a bogus proof term must be caught by the isDefEq x proof check at line 47-49 -- verify that a wrong-typed proof is rejected (.failedAssign) rather than accepted. None executed.
questions.cheat: Assuming the side condition (returning sorry-like proofs) makes every conditional rule fire and inflates 'simplification power'; the control is the false-hypothesis negative fixture whose answer must remain unchanged.

alternative_cuts: CUTS.md c14: the state-protection discipline (withPreservedCache, usedTheorems rollback, wellBehavedDischarge) is part of the memo-validity cluster, not of the discharger; Nyx bundled them at CUT-1 and expects to split at CUT-2
